passage:
A news website changed its comment rules. People could still disagree, but insults and personal attacks were removed.
Some readers called this censorship. Others said it made discussion readable again.
The website also added a reminder before posting: "Would you say this face to face?"
After the change, there were fewer comments, but more thoughtful ones.
A media class studied the case. Students learned that free expression and community standards often need balance.
An online space is still a space. If people fill it with shouting, others leave. Rules can limit harm and make better conversation possible.
